title: Attention: Issues, Sohlberg & Mateer Hierarchical Model, Sustained Attention
summary: Issues in attention; hierarchical model of attention (Sohlberg & Mateer); sustained attention; signal detection theory.
objectives: List the five levels of Sohlberg & Mateer's model.
Explain sustained attention and vigilance decrement.
revision: Five attention levels: Focused → Sustained → Selective → Alternating → Divided. Sustained attention = vigilance; vigilance decrement = decline over time.
traps: Vigilance decrement = performance declines over time.

notes.t: Attention involves selection, maintenance, and control of cognitive resources. Key issues include selective attention (focusing on one stimulus), divided attention (processing multiple stimuli), and sustained attention (maintaining focus over time).
Sustained attention (vigilance) is the ability to maintain focus on a task over an extended period. Performance typically declines over time (vigilance decrement).
UGC NET frequently tests the five levels of Sohlberg & Mateer's model and the vigilance decrement in sustained attention.
